Inscribed and signed, with one seal of the artistDated second month, dingchou year (1937)Dedicated to Shengjin (Gao Wenxian, 1913-1991)NOTE:This piece was executed in February 1937, when Master Hongyi was residing at Nanputuo Temple in Xiamen. Gao Wenxian was held in high regard by the Master, who even entrusted him with teaching some Buddhist instruction courses on his behalf. The verses transcribed here are by Gong Zizhen. In his inscription, the Master notes that he had recited this poem in childhood but had forgotten its opening line, revealing a subtle sense of nostalgic recollection. The full original poem reads:Unfinished, after all, the heart drifts vague and faint,In all things, better to embrace the flawed and incomplete.Singing on to where the setting sun meets mountains beyond mountains,Through the ages, who has ever escaped the lingering pull of feeling?Note: The phrase "where the setting sun meets mountains beyond mountains" evokes the lyrics of the famous song Farewell, composed by the Master before his renunciation. It is tempting to speculate that the song may also have been influenced by Gong Zizhen's verse—a point well worth pondering. The calligraphy features an open, spacious structure and restrained, lucid brushwork, embodying the austere clarity that emerged from the Master's integration of Vinaya practice into his art—a hallmark of his mature late style. Works of this kind, combining literary poetry, personal memory, and teacher-student affection, are rarely seen and are all the more precious.

The plan fell through, and he stayed at Nanputuo Temple. According to his chronological biography, in the same month the monk Purun cut his finger to draw blood; the Master wrote several sheets with it and distributed them to those with karmic affinity—the present piece likely being one of them. The inscription reads "year of jiaxu" and "the day of Śākyamuni Buddha's parinirvāṇa," indicating it was written on the fifteenth day of the second lunar month in 1934.In his early years, Hongyi wished to write sutras in blood, but was dissuaded by Master Yinguang due to his frail health. According to the inscription, this piece was written by Hongyi in 1934 using blood drawn from the finger of "Master Purun," and gifted to the layman Shengjin (Gao Wenxian). "Śramaṇa Purun" is Master Guangqia (1900–1994), originally named Zhaorun after ordination. He first met Hongyi at Nanputuo Temple in the winter of 1928, later attending to his daily needs and studying Buddhism under him. Hongyi renamed him Purun. He was a key protector of Hongyi during his later years in Fujian and later went to Singapore to spread the Dharma. This work is not only extremely rare but also bears witness to the intersection of Gao Wenxian with both Hongyi and Guangqia, holding significant artistic, historical, and documentary value.
